page: Microsoft Azure D96plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dpldsv6 server family. It is powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor with 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The hardware configuration features a low memory-to-core ratio, providing 192.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 5669 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance and memory bandwidth. The server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core metrics, including software compilation with Clang and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high across both small cached and large uncached read and write blocks. Conversely, single-core performance, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, falls within the average tier. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput also rank in the top tier.

Given the high physical core count and low memory density, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive RAM footprints. The bundled 5669 GB NVMe SSD provides high-capacity local storage, making it highly suitable for database operations, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded processing tasks. It is less suited for memory-intensive applications or workloads reliant on x86-specific instruction sets.
description: Microsoft Azure D96plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine from the Dpldsv6 family, configured with 96 dedicated physical cores on a 3.4 GHz Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. It features 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-optimized 2.0 GB per core ratio, and includes a 5669 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, this server delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance, exceptional memory bandwidth, and high-throughput database capabilities, as evidenced by outstanding Redis and static web serving benchmarks. Single-core performance and cryptographic execution remain in the average tier. This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for parallelized, compute-heavy tasks and high-speed database operations that require fast local storage but do not demand high memory-to-CPU ratios. It is ideal for software compilation, web serving, and multi-threaded data processing.
